title: Rendering Issues related to Sky Shader (Vulkan/ D3D12)
body: ### Tested versions - versions i testet: - godot 4.5.stable - godot 4.5.1.stable - godot 4.5.2.stable - godot 4.6.stable - godot 4.6.1.stable - godot 4.6.2.stable -> here the issue appears ### System information Godot v4.6.2.stable - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan/ D3D12 (Forward+) - dedicated AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT (Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.; 32.0.23033.1002) - AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D 8-Core Processor (16 threads) - 63.55 GiB memory ### Issue description So i just wanted to upgrade to the newest stable of godot 4.6.2 and i started to compile the engine with custom preference as usual. Normaly this just works flawlessly but this time the graphics of my game changed in some weird way without me doing anything to the project other then updating the engine. What i mean by that is; Almost everything looks normal except for the shadows and overall color saturation. Shadows appear much darker/dominant and some colors are oversaturated/not effected by light the right way. Godot 4.6.1.stable (how it should look like): Godot 4.6.2.stable: My attempts to resolve this so far: The first thing i did was checking my amd adrenalin software since i assumed this could be the result of an outdated driver. Turns out my driver is up to date. Checking again and still having the same issue as before. Next i tried clearing the shader cache but again the same result. Then i tried deleting and reloading the .godot folder. Once again the same result as before - did not help. I found some thread where someone was solving Vulkan issues by resetting an interfeering vulkan layer registry entry so i tried this aswell but still did not solve the problem. Then i tried the D3D12 backend but it would not work just like with Vulkan. Since all this did not help i thought maybe it is due to my custom version of godot i compiled from source. So i tried the normal Godot 4.6.2.stable stable version from the godot download page. But still the same problem. So i started testing from Godot 4.5.stable up to Godot 4.6.2.stable - normal Engine versions and my custom compiled ones. The last version that works without that issue is Godot 4.6.1.stable. The only trouble maker seems to be Godot 4.6.2.stable. Then i had thea idea that it could be due to some changes to how sky shader are processed. So i created a minimal project including the environment of my game and my sky shader. I made a scene using the default Sky as Sky and a scene using the sky shader for the Sky parameter. The scene with the custom sky (shader) has this graphic issues. The scene with the default sky looks just normal. So i assume it must be related to some change of shader processing but i don't know. I am not deep enaugh into shaders. with sky shader with normal sky I am out of ideas. Maybe i overlooked something but if anyone has an idea on how to fix this, please let me know. ### Steps to reproduce Since this could be a bug in my specific system i can only tell how i recreated: Using shader provided in the minal project as Sky in an Enviroment in a project of godot version 4.6.2.stable. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [testlighting.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26540442/testlighting.zip)
